facts.value: This is a wide-ranging and flexible degree. In first year, students select four subjects from a total of seventeen on offer. From second year onwards, students select two subjects to continue with for the remainder of their degree.

The Bachelor of Arts at UL offers unique subject combinations, a built-in work placement (cooperative education), and a mandatory semester of study abroad at one of UL’s partner institutions overseas.

Studying an arts degree opens up a broad world of career possibilities. Some arts students choose their courses and subjects with a specific career path in mind, such as the public sector, teaching, communications, or politics. However, many successful graduates started their arts degree uncertain about their exact future career but passionate about the subjects.

You will know that studying arts at UL might be a good fit for you if you want to choose from a wide range of subjects at an institution where you can benefit from real-world work experience and can live and study in another country; you wish to communicate your own ideas effectively and persuasively; you care about the world around you and want to understand the forces that shape people, society, culture, communication, and the physical world; you want to develop skills that will enhance your career and your contribution to society.
Individuals from/residing in EU/EFTA/UK countries
Apply via the Central Applications Office (CAO) for EU fee eligible applicants applying for first year undergraduate degree.
Offers cannot be issued until Round 1 offers after the Irish Leaving Certificate results are released.
Eligible applicants remain on the waiting list and may be offered in order of merit in later rounds, in accordance with CAO procedures.
Non-EU fee applicants and transfer applicants (post year 1) must apply directly to the University.
Applicants whose first language is not English must provide evidence of competence in a recognised English language test.
Acceptable level of English from European countries where English is presented as a subject.
Ordinary Level Grade D or above in English.
580 (paper-based) or 90 (internet-based).
Minimum score of 6.5 with no less than 6.0 in any component.
Grade C1 in English Test for Academic and Professional Purposes.
Grade C or above in English Language/GCSE English Language.
Proficiency Certificate, Grade C or better (CEFR Level C1 or C2), Advanced Certificate, Grade C or better (CEFR Level C1 or C2), or First Certificate, Grade A (CEFR Level C1).

Oxford Delegacy of Local Examinations: Grade C, Cambridge Local Examinations Syndicate: School Certificate Pass 1-6, University of London Entrance and School Examinations Council: School Certificate Pass 1-6.
Minimum score of 61 (with no section score below 59).
Overall minimum 140. Individual skills 125.
B2 Communicator High Pass with no less than 33 in each skill.
Minimum requirement will be a DET score of 120 with at least 110 in each sub score.
The Qualifications and Assessments section of the CAO handbook provides information on documentation or evidence you may need to supply to support your application.

facts.value: Students have the opportunity to spend a semester abroad in one of our 300+ partner universities around the world.
Typically for one semester
Students do not pay tuition fees at the host University during the semester abroad.
Any student enrolled in a full-time course at UL, leading to a degree or postgraduate qualification.
Typically in their 2nd or 3rd year
Most humanities degrees include an integrated Erasmus academic placement.
Students on the ERASMUS+ programme receive a mobility grant of between €230-280 per month.
The grant assists with added costs such as travel expenses and higher general costs of living in the host country.
The Erasmus grant is not means-tested and should not affect any other local grant funding.
There is no specific grant available for non-EU exchange placements.
Studying abroad can enhance skills and employability.
UL was awarded Best Erasmus Programme by the Irish Education Awards in both 2018 and 2019.
Approximately 500 UL students study abroad at European partner institutions each year.

facts.value: You must have been living in an EU/EEA member state or Switzerland for at least 3 of the 5 years before starting your course.
You must be a citizen of an EU/EEA member state or Switzerland or have official refugee status.

You must be a first time full-time undergraduate (Exceptions are provided for students who hold a Level 6 or Level 7 qualification and are progressing to a Level 8 course in the same general area of study).
You must be undertaking a full-time undergraduate course of at least 2 years' duration.
You cannot be undertaking a repeat year of study at the same level unless evidence of exceptional circumstances eg serious illness is provided (in which case this condition may be waived).
You satisfy all three categories (1, 2 and 3) and therefore are eligible for the Higher Education Authority’s Free Fees scheme.
You satisfy both the citizenship and residency criteria but fail to satisfy the course requirements and are liable to EU fees.
You do not meet either the citizenship or residency criteria and are therefore liable to Non EU fees.
